note: Discovery leads for marketing topic workers (phase 2). LITERACY level: teach what each concept IS and WHY it matters, with original examples. Business context (introduction-to-business already covers marketing at survey level — reuse its source ids where URLs are identical). No advertising-industry hype; no unverifiable statistics; every claim source-verified.

tierA.useFor: THE backbone — ch. 1 (marketing defined), 3 (market segmentation/positioning), 4 (consumer behavior), 5 (marketing research), 7 (branding), 8-11 (marketing mix), 14-16 (promotion/advertising/PR). openstax.org blocks curl — read sections via Wayback captures of the canonical section URLs
marketing definition (the AMA definition), marketing research, brand — official professional body
advertising truth-in-advertising basics, ethics-in-marketing (deceptive practices), endorsement guides (general)
market research statistics (general demographic facts, time-anchored)

tierB.useFor: classic frameworks (STP, 4Ps) — cite via secondary reliable sources, not the book itself
concept explainers (positioning, segmentation, brand equity, marketing mix)
terms (often JS-walled — Wayback or CFI instead)
digital-marketing mechanics (SEO, email, social, content) — Tier C/D unless corroborated

cautions: FRAMEWORK FIDELITY: the 4 Ps, STP (segment-target-position), AIDA, and the classic brand-equity definitions are standard textbook material — attribute to their canonical sources (AMA, OpenStax, Kotler via reliable secondary). Never present a framework as invented.

NO HYPE: no 'marketing is everything' claims; no unverifiable ROI statistics; no fake case studies. Original fictional examples only (the established cast: Meadow Bakery, Harbor Books, Riverbend Books, Riverside Cycles, Gable Street Roasters, MetroFrame, Bluebird Bakery, Rosa's bakery, Harborline Coffee).

NO PSYCHOLOGICAL MANIPULATION CONTENT: consumer-behavior teaches what factors shape buying decisions (culture, social, personal, psychological — the classic four) factually; no 'how to manipulate customers' framing.

DIGITAL MARKETING: SEO/email/social/content mechanics taught factually (what the practice IS, how it works, general best practices); no promises of rankings or results; no unverifiable industry stats.
ETHICS: truth-in-advertising (FTC), deception, targeting vulnerable groups — factual; no policy positions.

Scope: introduction-to-business's marketing lesson and advertising lesson are SIBLING-survey content — reference, don't repeat; consumer-behavior/psychology overlaps with the psychology subject (reference only).

Distribute question answer keys EVENLY across A/B/C/D (≥1 C, ≥1 D per topic; max 3 of 5 per slot). Verify keys from the file yourself. BANNED: 'Which statement best defines X used in this lesson?' stems — write scenario questions (e.g. 'A bakery wants to reach new parents in its neighborhood. Which segmentation base is it using?').
